q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of stainless steel surgical instruments?
title: Surgical instrument carbon footprint
short: Multiply the stainless steel per instrument, including forging and machining scrap, by your steel supplier's per-kg figure. Add forging fuel, heat treatment, machining, polishing and passivation, cleaning and packing, then divide plant energy by instruments passed.

ul: Martensitic or austenitic stainless bar or blanks by weight.
Drop forging and trimming, with furnace or induction heating.
Grinding, polishing, passivation and ultrasonic cleaning.

p: Report per instrument type, since a scalpel handle and a retractor differ widely in steel weight.

example.title: Worked example: instrument unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 19,240 / 50,000 = 0.385 kg CO2 per instrument
Add stainless steel for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
